responses.response: In this repo, bootstrap projects/payments/ by following the shape already visible in projects/template/: create projects/payments/likec4.config.json, one model file such as system-model.c4, and one view file such as system-views.c4; that is the minimum clean setup. In the config, give the project its own name/title, include the payments files plus only the shared spec files and images it actually needs, and keep payments-owned business elements inside projects/payments/, not under projects/shared/. Add an ADR/ folder only if you want the same decision-record convention as the template project.

Not in the shared specifications area. The visible shared area is spec-oriented (spec-*.c4, a cheat sheet, and images), so putting paymentsCore there would mix business model with technical specification. Keep paymentsCore in the payments project. Put backOfficeUser in shared only if it is a truly cross-project actor with one canonical meaning everywhere, and even then place it in a separate shared domain/common-model file rather than in spec files. Cross-project references should use one canonical definition and be consumed by inclusion or by an integration/landscape project; avoid duplicating the same actor or system in multiple projects or referencing another project's private internals directly.

Not by itself. Use this workflow for project boundaries, ownership, and deciding what is shared versus project-local, but combine it with a configuration-focused step for include paths and image aliases, because those are config concerns rather than repository-organization concerns. In practice: create the new project structure first, then update that project's config so it resolves the correct shared files and image roots.

Do not dump everything into one shared bucket. Separate technical conventions from reusable business models, but keep the structure shallow: keep spec files and assets in the existing shared spec area, and add one small shared-domain or common-model area for truly reusable actors and systems. Project-owned models should still live inside each project folder. A good rule is: spec files define language, styles, and conventions; shared domain files define canonical reusable business elements; project folders define local models and views. That avoids both the junk-drawer problem and an over-engineered folder maze.
